title: Locality constraints and proofchain for tenant API routing
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers operating under strict data locality and sovereignty rules need first-class controls to limit where Hosted API request payloads, cached artifacts, and derived outputs may transit or be stored. Existing region pinning controls are terse and hard to reason about when combined with fallback routing, autoscaling, and cross-region cache hits. We propose adding: 1) a policy layer of locality constraints (allow/deny by region, region groups, and tenancy-affinity levels), 2) a tenant-level fingerprint (locality profile) that persists with request metadata, and 3) an automated \"proofchain\" evidence pipeline that snapshots routing decisions, retention TTLs, and cryptographically-signed export bundles for audits. This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the Hosted API surface and the evidence packaging that auditors will consume.
acceptance_criteria: Product API: Admins can create locality constraint policies scoped to tenant or route that specify allowed regions, disallowed regions, and an ordered fallback list.
Runtime enforcement: Requests from a pinned tenant are routed only to nodes that satisfy the active locality constraint; any forced fallback must be logged and flagged as a policy violation.
Tenant fingerprint: Each tenant has a locality profile stored in control plane metadata with a human-readable summary and machine-readable policy ID.

Evidence pipeline: For any policy change or routing fallback, the system generates an exportable proof bundle (JSON manifest + signed routing trace + retention snapshot) within 24 hours and makes it available for download from the tenant console and via an API endpoint.
UI: Console shows active locality constraints, last 30 days of enforcement events, and a one-click 'Generate Evidence Bundle' button.
Compatibility: New controls work with Dedicated and Private deployments. For Private, data plane will accept and honor policy tokens from control plane; docs updated accordingly.
Tests: E2E test that simulates multi-region outage and verifies that routing respects deny-lists and that the proofchain bundle contains the fallback event with signed artifacts.
Security: Security review completed and KMS keys used to sign proof bundles; access controls restrict evidence downloads to allowed tenant admins.
Docs: Confluence design doc and API reference published; migration guide for existing region pinning policies provided.
work_breakdown: PM: finalize policy model and priority semantics (allow vs deny, precedence, expiration).
Design: wireframes for locality constraint editor, enforcement timeline UI, and evidence bundle UX.
ENG-Core: implement policy model in control plane, tenant fingerprint storage, and API endpoints.
ENG-Runtime: enforce routing at the router level, add enforcement hooks to autoscaler, and emit signed traces.
ENG-Observability: create evidence bundling service that collects traces, retention snapshots, and signs artifacts via KMS.
QA: create simulation harness for multi-region failures and tenancy-affinity tests.
Docs: author admin guide and migration path; update private deployment runbook.

notes_for_engineering: Runtime must be able to check policy metadata without adding a blocking network hop in the fast path. Suggested approach: embed signed policy token in tenant metadata refreshed via control plane push; runtime validates token signature and version locally. Also include an 'event-only' mode for canary that emits enforcement logs without blocking traffic.
migration_notes: Existing region pinning rules will be imported into the new locality policy model with a default allow/deny mapping; provide a one-click migration utility in the Console and a CLI for private deployments.
qa_plan: 1) Simulate tenant with allow-only EU regions and issue requests from US region to validate rejection; 2) Trigger region failure and verify fallback logging + proofbundle contains signed trace; 3) Validate access control for evidence download using tenant admin and non-admin accounts.
notes: This ticket aims to unify the UX and auditability story for data locality without compromising runtime latency objectives. The evidence 'proofchain' is intentionally minimal (signed JSON+trace) for now; future iterations may support full PKCS#7 bundles.
